title: Generic torus quotient of a semiabelian scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-sc-group-scheme] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point. Then the schematic closure $T\subseteq G$ of the maximal torus of $G_\eta$ is a closed subgroup scheme which is a torus over $S$ (fppf locally on $S$ isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\geq0$), and there are a smooth separated commutative group scheme $H\to S$ of finite presentation and a homomorphism $q:G\to H$ which is the fppf quotient of $G$ by $T$. The map $q$ is a faithfully flat $T$-torsor, $H_\eta$ is an abelian variety over $\kappa(\eta)$, and $H$ has semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]; in particular every fibre of $H\to S$ is connected. The torus, quotient, base-change and morphism conventions are [def-pc-base-change] [def-sc-abelian-variety] [def-pc-fppf-site] [def-sc-gm-ga] [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-sfb-fppf-group-quotient-presentation].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.7 and Chapter I, §2; Raynaud IX 2.4 and Faltings–Chai I, Proposition 2.9.

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(\eta)$. The fibre hypothesis gives the extension over an algebraic closure of $K$. Its middle group is integral by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$, so the geometric-connectedness hypothesis of [lem-sfb-geometric-semiabelian-split-quotient] holds. That node supplies a finite Galois extension $E/K$ and $1\to V_E\to G_E\to A_E\to1$, with $V_E$ split and $A_E$ abelian. The torus $V_E$ is unique: after an algebraic closure, any torus in $G_E$ maps to zero in $A_E$ by [lem-sfb-torus-abelian-hom-vanishing], hence lies in $V_E$; two candidates therefore contain one another. Equality of their ideals is detected by a faithfully flat field extension. Thus every Galois conjugate preserves $V_E$ as a closed subgroup. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-closed-subscheme-descent] to obtain a closed subgroup $V\subset G_\eta$. Its affineness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine]; it is a $K$-torus because it becomes a split torus over $E$. The same inclusion argument after a common algebraic closure proves that $V$ is the maximal torus. Denote it by $T_\eta$. Explicitly, tensoring any ideal inclusion with a field extension is injective by [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective]; [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] supplies the surjective field base changes used to descend connectedness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generic-toric-abstract-good-reduction] to $V=T_\eta$. Its hypotheses hold over the original normal integral locally Noetherian base, not merely over a trait. Obtain the abstract affine faithfully flat torus $P\to S$ and $\alpha:P_\eta\simeq T_\eta$. A torus has semiabelian geometric fibres: over an algebraically closed field use its split presentation and the trivial abelian variety, with quotient to the identity point. Thus $P$ and $G$ meet all the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-normal-semiabelian-hom-extension]. Extend $P_\eta\xrightarrow{\alpha}T_\eta\hookrightarrow G_\eta$ to $i:P\to G$.

proof.text: The generic homomorphism $i_\eta$ is a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-hom-generic-closed-rigidity] to the already constructed $i$, and identify $P$ with its closed subgroup image $T\subseteq G$. To identify this closed image with the specified schematic closure, first note that $\eta\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and schematically dominant: on every nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $R\hookrightarrow K$ is injective. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] with $U=\eta$, $X=S$ and the flat map $P\to S$. It gives that $P_\eta$ is schematically dense in $P$. A closed subscheme of $G$ containing $T_\eta$ therefore contains $T$: its defining ideal restricts to zero on $P_\eta$, hence to zero on $P$. Since $T$ itself is closed with generic fibre $T_\eta$, it is the schematic closure. This also proves the subgroup assertion and all torus assertions, including rank zero.

proof.text: Let $T$ act on $G$ by translation. On every test scheme $U$, $tg=g$ implies $t=1$ by group cancellation and injectivity of $T(U)\to G(U)$, so the action is free. The acting group is flat and locally of finite presentation by its torus structure. Apply [lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient] with $B=S$ and $Z=G$. It gives the algebraic space $F=G/T$, an fppf locally surjective, flat, locally finitely presented $p:G\to F$, and $T\times_SG\simeq G\times_FG$. Commutativity gives a group law on $F$: locally lift two sections to $g_1,g_2$ and take the class of $g_1g_2$. Replacing lifts by $t_1g_1,t_2g_2$ changes the product by $t_1t_2$, so the result is well-defined and glues as a sheaf section; inverse and identity are defined in the same way. Their identities are checked on the local lifts.

source.place: Tag 06PH, lemma-quotient-free-action, as stated by lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient; explicit quotient group law.

proof.text: For every geometric point $s$, the given semiabelian extension makes $G_s$ integral by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$. In particular these geometric fibres are connected, and so is every ordinary fibre $G_x$ ($x\in S$): it is the image of the connected scheme $G_{\bar x}$ for an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$, under the projection that is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and continuous. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-smooth-group-local-ample-line] to $G$: the normal locally Noetherian base, smooth separated finite-presentation group and connected fibres required there have all been checked. This supplies the affine open cover and ample modules required by [lem-sfb-relatively-ample-subtorus-quotient-schematicity]. Apply that node to the algebraic space $F$ of step 4. Write $H$ for its representing smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation, and $q$ for $p$ as a scheme map. The flat locally surjective map of step 4 is faithfully flat, and its relation isomorphism is exactly $(g,t)\mapsto(g,gt)$, after switching the factors. Its unit fibre is $T$: a section of $G$ maps to the identity precisely when fppf locally it is a section of $T$, and membership in this represented closed subgroup glues. Thus the kernel, local-surjectivity, relation and sheafification clauses of [def-sfb-fppf-group-quotient-presentation] hold. This is the required $T$-torsor and fppf quotient.

source.place: Chapter VI, §§1–2 (relatively quasi-projective homogeneous spaces), and Chapter IX, §2 (subtori). WANTED: original text and precise quotient representability statement; independently formulated supporting lemma.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed geometric residue field $k$. The local lifts and the relation isomorphism in step 4 remain valid over $k$: pull back their covering families using [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Hence $H_k=G_k/T_k$ as fppf sheaves. Choose $1\to R\to G_k\to A\to1$ from the given semiabelian-fibre hypothesis, with $R=\mathbf G_m^n$. The composite $T_k\to A$ vanishes by [lem-sfb-torus-abelian-hom-vanishing], so $T_k$ factors through the kernel $R$. Its closed immersion into $G_k$ makes this factorization a closed immersion into $R$ (it is the base change along $R\hookrightarrow G_k$). By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], its character map $\mathbf Z^n\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z^r$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], the kernel $L$ is finite free: the surjection splits by choosing lifts of the standard basis, and a subgroup of the finite free abelian group $\mathbf Z^n$ is finite free. Now [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-quotient-character-kernel] gives $R/T_k=D_k(L)$, a split torus. Local lifts in $G_k$ identify the kernel of $H_k\to A$ with $R/T_k$: a lift maps to the identity of $A$ exactly when it lies in $R$, and changing a lift changes it by $T_k$. Every section of $A$ fppf locally lifts to $G_k$, hence to $H_k$. Thus $1\to D_k(L)\to H_k\to A\to1$ is an exact fppf extension. This is precisely a semiabelian geometric fibre.

proof.text: Return to $E/K$ from step 1. The equality $T_E=V_E$ makes both $H_E$ and $A_E$ the fppf quotient of $G_E$ by the same kernel. The comparison is explicit: fppf locally lift a section to $G_E$, take its image in the other quotient, and glue. Two lifts differ by a kernel section, so the map is well-defined; doing this in both directions gives inverse homomorphisms. The base change of each covering is an fppf covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Therefore $H_E\simeq A_E$ is proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-morphism-fpqc-descent] to the finite faithfully flat field cover $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. It gives properness of $H_\eta$. Smoothness and commutativity were supplied in step 5, and geometric connectedness follows from the semiabelian extensions of step 6: [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$ makes every geometric fibre $H_k$ integral. Consequently $H_\eta$ is an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety], and all geometric fibres, hence all fibres, of $H\to S$ are connected. Smoothness under field base change is [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2); for the last connectedness assertion use the continuous surjection from an algebraic-closure fibre, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].
